title: Using Claude Opus 5.5 as your daily driver for knowledge work
summary: This guide recommends Opus 5.5 for research, analysis, memos, spreadsheets, and decks, and Opus 5.5 is now the default on Pro, Max, Ultra, and Team plans. Pricing is $4/$20 per million tokens versus $2/$10 for Sonnet 5.5, and a financial modeling task took 63 minutes versus 93 for Opus 5 at half the cost, with Medium effort matching or beating Opus 5 at High. Tips include asking for finished files, connecting work files, and stating the goal and output up front.

title: Using a "chaos loop" to harden the Claude Docs launch: 60 server errors across billions of requests
summary: For two weeks before the Claude Docs launch on September 16, 2026, Claude ran continuously on staging, load-testing the service, reading telemetry, and deploying fixes while humans approved irreversible changes. A 3 GB memory issue in one doc was fixed with copy-on-write (about 180 MB), cutting the capacity estimate from 500+ pods to about 50. The launch reached 4.6M docs by September 22 with 60 server errors over 2B requests, 629 production rollouts, and no rollbacks, at about $125k in inference at list price.

title: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification
summary: About 90% of the Claude Code team's code is written and reviewed by Claude, with preferred tests being end-to-end, property, and differential tests, plus a verify skill that boots and drives the app and escalates to a human after three failed rounds. Guardrails keep changes from modifying the checks that judge them, read REVIEW.md from the base branch, start gates in observe mode, and never skip or retry flaky tests. The article argues verification is what enables delegation and parallel agents, shifting the engineer's role to defining "done" and reviewing evidence.

title: Building always-on agents
summary: This guide covers stateful, proactive agents that keep context across sessions and act unsupervised, mostly sleeping and waking for short runs, built from five primitives: event inbox, timers, durable memory, permissions, and outbox. Newer models judge intent and check-in timing better, and long-horizon work is cheaper (Opus 5.5 used 78% less per solved task than Opus 5 on one benchmark), while permissions carry the most risk. Its core advice is to start quiet and earn the user's attention.

title: J. Crew brings its signature approach to styling to life with Claude
summary: J.Crew launched Style Advisor, an AI stylist on JCrew.com for US women's and men's shoppers that turns a described occasion into complete outfits drawn from its photo shoots, refinable in chat. It was built with Claude Code, using a larger model for planning, Sonnet for conversation decisions, and Haiku for quick tasks. Next steps include personalization from preferences and purchase history, plus more markets and lines.

title: Introducing Claude for Manufacturing
summary: Claude for Manufacturing is a plugin with 17 skills and four connectors (Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365, and Oracle NetSuite) that drafts quotes, quality reports, and supplier requests from a manufacturer's own records. Its skills cover failed-inspection investigation, breakdown diagnosis, sourcing, design comparison, and production reporting, and the Infor plugin can make approved changes. It is available on Team and Enterprise plans, humans approve all work, and it does not operate equipment.
